To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the properties of the high-conductance mechanosensitive channels in the membrane patches from Bacillus subtils are altered by DNA in a manner that indicates a direct interaction between the two.
DNA interacts with mechanosensitive channels of B. subtilis in native membrane patches, and that this interaction results in the translocation of DNA across the membrane.
the high-conductance mechanosensitive channel of Bacillus subilitis interacts with DNA and that the interaction takes place in both artificial and native membranes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the interaction between DNA and mechanosensitive channels in the membrane patches of B. subtilis.
the identification of the molecular nature of mechanosensitive channels in bacteria.
the study of DNA interactions with mechanosensitive channels of B. subtilis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the large mechanosensitive channel observed by patch-clampting bacterial cells is a protein complex capable of forming large transmembrane pores that is also involved in the translocation of DNA across the bacterial membrane.
the DNA interacts with the same channels in the native membrane and in planar lipid bilayers, and that this interaction results in the translocation of the DNA in the two systems.
, in the case of B. subtilis, mechanosensitive channels are a component of the DNA translocation apparatus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the same channel protein is involved in two distinct processes, one related to the transport of proteins across the membrane and the other to DNA translocation, which may occur in vivo in response to mechanical stress.
the DNA channel complex, which is the key element in the translocation of genetic material, is a native component of the bacterial membrane.
DNA interacts with the same channels in both systems and that this interaction may have a functional significance in the translocation of the DNA through the membrane.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the large mechanosensitive ion channels in B. subtilis membranes are not just passive pores, but are also capable of specific interactions with other membrane constituents.
the mechanosensitive channels that are responsible for the transmembrane DNA transport observed in the artificial membranes also mediate DNA translocation in the native membrane.
the interaction between DNA and large mechanosensitive channel-forming proteins in the native membrane is a common feature of bacterial transport systems.
